faithfulness.note: Every constant of the profile is an estimate and the geometry is an assumption of the profile: the bundle exercises the estimated-evidence path and is never cited as a chip.

notes: allow_coalescing and allow_neuron_splitting are true, an assumption of the estimated point like its geometry: the profile describes no real chip, and its digital cores are assumed to add partial sums and split outputs across cores, as the framework's study grid declares (every tier-0 cell of that grid declares both); a study that assumes otherwise declares either through target_overrides with a note. onchip_arithmetic declares the lane subset L, E and P (on by default for value-domain chips, owner 2026-10-15; the off ablation declares classes [] through target_overrides with a note): ReLU as the law's clamp, a fused add and a requantizing average pool run on chip when the program is on the integer path (readout_law); a float value program keeps its host ops. The lane block is ng45_os_lane (an output-stage lane synthesized at 45 nm and 1.1 V, arith_toggle.md section 6, estimated; the resolver scales its area by node^2 and its energy by node x V^2 to this target's node, naming the factor in each row), one lane per 64 output columns, so 4 lanes per core (256 output columns per core). The certified function applies one ADC to each column's fused accumulator, while the cost model prices one conversion per array: the two are identical where adc_bits reaches an array's accumulator width, and below it the checked accuracy is not the priced chip's (per-array ADC, W47, not built).
